record.paper_title: Some Properties of and Open Problems on Hessian Nilpotent Polynomials
record.context_brief: Graph-theoretic criteria for the Vanishing Conjecture
record.original_question: Let C^n carry the standard C-bilinear form <., .>, and let X(C^n) be the set of isotropic vectors alpha with <alpha, alpha> = 0. Let P(z) be a homogeneous harmonic polynomial of degree d >= 2 over C written as P(z) = sum_{i=1}^k h_{alpha_i}(z)^d, where h_alpha(z) = <alpha, z> and each alpha_i lies in X(C^n). Define the graph G(P) to have vertex set {1, 2, ..., k}, with vertices i and j joined by an edge exactly when <alpha_i, alpha_j> is nonzero; regard G(P) as labeled when an edge i--j is assigned the value <alpha_i, alpha_j>, and in the even-degree variant when the edge label is h_{alpha_i}(z)^((d-2)/2) <alpha_i, alpha_j> h_{alpha_j}(z)^((d-2)/2). What necessary or sufficient conditions on this labeled graph G(P) ensure that the Vanishing Conjecture holds for the homogeneous Hessian nilpotent polynomial P(z), meaning Delta^m(P(z)^(m+1)) = 0 for all sufficiently large m?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.1. (Vanishing Conjecture) Let Delta := sum_{i=1}^n D_i^2 be the Laplace operator of C[z]. Then, for any HN polynomial P (z) (of homogeneous of degree d = 4), Delta^m P^{m+1} (z) = 0 when m >> 0.
The set of vertices of G(P ) will be the set of positive integers [k] := {1, 2, . . . , k}. The vertices i and j of G(P ) are connected by an edge iff <alpha_i , alpha_j> != 0.
we may also label edges of G(P ) by assigning <alpha_i , alpha_j> or (h_{alpha_i}^{(d-2)/2} <alpha_i , alpha_j> h_{alpha_j}^{(d-2)/2}), when d is even
Open Problem 8.4. (b) Find some necessary or sufficient conditions on the (labeled) graph G(P ) such that the VC holds for the homogeneous HN polynomial P (z).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Equip $\mathbb{C}^n$ with the standard symmetric $\mathbb{C}$-bilinear form $\langle \cdot,\cdot\rangle$ defined by $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^n u_i v_i$. Let $X(\mathbb{C}^n):=\{\alpha\in\mathbb{C}^n:\langle\alpha,\alpha\rangle=0\}$ be the set of isotropic vectors, and for $\alpha\in\mathbb{C}^n$ set $h_\alpha(z):=\langle\alpha,z\rangle$. Let $\Delta:=\sum_{i=1}^n \partial_{z_i}^2$ be the Laplace operator on $\mathbb{C}[z_1,\dots,z_n]$.

A polynomial $P(z)\in\mathbb{C}[z_1,\dots,z_n]$ is called Hessian nilpotent (HN) if its Hessian matrix $\mathrm{Hess}(P)=(\partial_{z_i}\partial_{z_j}P)$ is nilpotent as a matrix over $\mathbb{C}[z_1,\dots,z_n]$. The Vanishing Conjecture (VC) asserts that for every homogeneous HN polynomial $P(z)$ one has $\Delta^m(P(z)^{m+1})=0$ for all sufficiently large $m$.

Suppose $P(z)$ is a homogeneous harmonic polynomial (i.e.\ $\Delta P=0$) of degree $d\ge 2$ which can be written as
$$P(z)=\sum_{i=1}^k h_{\alpha_i}(z)^d, \qquad \alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_k\in X(\mathbb{C}^n).$$
Associate to such a representation the graph $G(P)$ with vertex set $[k]=\{1,2,\dots,k\}$ and an edge between $i\ne j$ exactly when $\langle\alpha_i,\alpha_j\rangle\ne 0$. Consider $G(P)$ as a labeled graph by assigning to each edge $i\!-\!j$ either the label $\langle\alpha_i,\alpha_j\rangle$, or, when $d$ is even, the label $h_{\alpha_i}(z)^{(d-2)/2}\,\langle\alpha_i,\alpha_j\rangle\,h_{\alpha_j}(z)^{(d-2)/2}$.

Problem: Determine necessary or sufficient conditions on the labeled graph $G(P)$ that ensure the Vanishing Conjecture holds for $P(z)$, i.e.\ that $\Delta^m(P(z)^{m+1})=0$ for all sufficiently large $m$.
artifact.status_search_result: The Vanishing Conjecture remains open in general (it implies, and is closely related to, the Jacobian Conjecture). Subsequent work has investigated graph-theoretic structure of representations of HN polynomials as sums of powers of isotropic linear forms and obtained partial results (e.g.\ showing certain graphs such as lines and cycles cannot arise), but no complete characterization of labeled graphs $G(P)$ guaranteeing VC is known.

status_evidence.title: Hessian Nilpotent Polynomials and the Jacobian Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: The Jacobian Conjecture has been reduced to the Vanishing Conjecture on Laplace operators and Hessian nilpotent polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: The Vanishing Conjecture is a known reformulation underlying the Jacobian Conjecture and remains open.

status_evidence.title: Two results on homogeneous Hessian nilpotent polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Structural results on graphs associated to Hessian nilpotent polynomials, including that lines and cycles cannot appear as such graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial graph-theoretic obstructions are known; the general characterization remains open.

status_evidence.title: A few remarks on the Generalized Vanishing Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Further remarks and partial progress on the Vanishing Conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature continues to treat VC as an open conjecture with only partial progress.
